subject: A problem with a model identification and convergence

messages.author: e6501b66d16cfb0c
messages.subject: A problem with a model identification and convergence
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to fit a model with 2 exogenous formative LVs. LV1 has 3 indicators that form it, and LV2 has 4 indicators. A third LV (LV3) is reflective and has 5 indicators and is the endogenous variable.

The steps I have done so far included the following:

1- Checked for SEM assumptions.

2- CFA in my reflective latent variable (here I found that the model do not converge), I tried to remove some indicators and see if the issue will improve but the best result I received is negative variance error.

the code I used for cfa:

model.c <- '

LV3 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5

'
fit<- cfa(model.c data=dataset)
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)

3- I tried to scale the LV by

LV3 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5

'
fit<- cfa(model.c data=dataset, std.lv = TRUE)
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)

This solution produced results and x1 and x5 are statistically insignificant so I dropped them

4- I now used the following code to fit my full SEM model

model <- '

LV1 <~ x6 + x7 + x8

LV2 <~ x9 + x10 + x11 + x12

LV3 =~ x2 + x3 + x4

###### Path Model ######

LV3 ~ LV1 + LV2

'
fit<- sem(model.c data=dataset, std.lv = TRUE)
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)


However, I always receive this message:

Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

What should I do?!

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: A problem with a model identification and convergence
parts: First you need to add some constraints and some more covariances to your model. This is identified:

model <- '
LV1 <~ x6 + x7 + x8
LV2 <~ x9 + x10 + x11 + x12
LV3 =~ x2 + x3 + x4
###### Path Model ######

LV3 ~ 1 * LV1 + 1 * LV2
LV1 ~~ 0 * LV1
LV2 ~~ 0 * LV2
LV2 ~~ 0 * LV1
x6 ~~ x7 + x8
x7 ~~ x8
x9 ~~ x10 + x11 + x12
x10 ~~ x11 + x12
x11 ~~ x12

'

LV 1 and LV2 need to have a variance of zero, or the model isn't identified (that's always true of formative indicators with one arrow coming out of them). 

You should also add covariances between the indicators of the formative variables. 

The crux of the problem that this is a pretty weird model. LV1 and LV2 aren't doing anything. 



LV1 and LV2 aren't  doing anything. 

Here's a model where I take them out, and put the paths from the formative indicators directly to LV3.


model2 <- '
LV3 ~ x6 + x7 + x8
LV3 ~ x9 + x10 + x11 + x12

LV3 =~ x2 + x3 + x4
###### Path Model ######

x6 ~~ x7 + x8
x7 ~~ x8
x9 ~~ x10 + x11 + x12
x10 ~~ x11 + x12
x11 ~~ x12

'

Here's the original fit:
> summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
lavaan (0.5-23.1097) converged normally after  22 iterations

  Number of observations                          1000

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic              916.291
  Degrees of freedom                                26
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000

Here's the new fit:

> summary(fit2)
lavaan (0.5-23.1097) converged normally after  22 iterations

  Number of observations                          1000

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic              916.291
  Degrees of freedom                                26
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000



And all of the lack of fit is coming from the fact that the formative indicators of the two formative latents are not allowed to correlate.

Add those correlations, and the fit is perfect. (I don't understand where the model gets 14df from).


model3 <- '
LV3 ~ x6 + x7 + x8
LV3 ~ x9 + x10 + x11 + x12

LV3 =~ x2 + x3 + x4
###### Path Model ######

x6 ~~ x7 + x8
x7 ~~ x8
x9 ~~ x10 + x11 + x12
x10 ~~ x11 + x12
x11 ~~ x12
x6 ~~ x9 + x10 + x11 + x12
x7 ~~ x9 + x10 + x11 + x12
x8 ~~ x9 + x10 + x11 + x12

> summary(fit3, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
lavaan (0.5-23.1097) converged normally after  36 iterations

  Number of observations                          1000

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic                0.000
  Degrees of freedom                                14
  P-value (Chi-square)                           1.000



Generally, formative indicators are weird, and to be avoided unless you have a really good reason to have them. I don't *think* this model tells you anything that you couldn't have known with regression.

Also, it's much easier for people to answer if you can provide a reproducible example. It doesn't have to be your data. Here's what I used:

library(lavaan)

d <- matrix(rep(0.7, 144), nrow = 12)
diag(d) <- 1  
colnames(d) <- rownames(d) <- paste0("x", 1:12)

model <- '
LV1 <~ x6 + x7 + x8
LV2 <~ x9 + x10 + x11 + x12
LV3 =~ x2 + x3 + x4
###### Path Model ######
LV3 ~ 1 * LV1 + 1 * LV2
LV1 ~~ 0 * LV1
LV2 ~~ 0 * LV2
LV2 ~~ 0 * LV1
x6 ~~ x7 + x8
x7 ~~ x8
x9 ~~ x10 + x11 + x12
x10 ~~ x11 + x12
x11 ~~ x12

'

fit <- sem(model, sample.cov = d, sample.nobs = 1000)
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)


Hope that's helpful. 

Jeremy

messages.subject: Re: A problem with a model identification and convergence
parts: Having thought about this some more, I've realized where the df are coming from. The model is testing whether the relationship between the predictor variables (x6 to x12)  and the outcomes (x1 to x3) are scaled equally to the relationship between the endogenous latent variable (LV3). Hence df = (3-1) * 7. (My fake data tricked me.)
